newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of Korea chief sees contact with North soon.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea chief sees contact with North soon.

text.p: Some form of interaction would take place between North and South Korea before long, Kyung Shik Lee, governor of the Bank of Korea, told a financial conference on Friday.

"In my personal view, it's not so long (before we have) some kind of interaction between North and South," Kyung said during a question and answer session on the financial implications of the unification of North and South Korea.
"This is a very difficult question, it's not a question for central bankers, it's a question for politicians," Kyung said.
Kyung said he hoped the Communist-ruled North and the South would make contact in a peaceful way. "Nobody can predict it, even imagine, when and how," he said.
Kyung was speaking on a panel at a conference jointly organised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
